title: Herodotus takes part in the Egyptian mystery cults and then stays silent about them

tellings.quote: Heroditus talks about these mystery cults in Egypt and he speculates on like I wonder what's going on here and then while he's in Egypt he's allowed to participate in them and then he doesn't talk about it again.

plain: The Greek historian Herodotus, writing about Egypt, wondered aloud about the country's mystery cults, secret religious rites that only initiates could join, and then, while he was there, was allowed to take part in them and never wrote about them again. The researcher Luke Caverns tells Michels this, citing Herodotus but no particular passage. The point, as he tells it, is that the silence suggests Herodotus learned something he would not or could not share.
